messages:
Amy Chen: heads-up — we need to pick a canonical span name + semantic attrs for all LLM request traces. Right now eng/runtime, eng-platform, and eng-ml all use slightly different keys, which kills dashboard joins. Can we land on something minimal and extensible?

Matt R: +1. Proposal: span.name = "redwood.infer.request" (single span per API request at the gateway level). Then add sub-spans for batching / model-inference if teams want them. Keeps service-dashboards simple.

Priya Singh: curious about attributes. Suggested minimal set: 
```
service.name = "redwood-inference"
span.name = "redwood.infer.request"
redwood.model.name = "gpt-4o-mini"
redwood.model.version = "2026-03-01"
redwood.model.variant = "int8"
redwood.request.tokens.input = 34
redwood.request.tokens.output = 210
redwood.cache.hit = true
redwood.routing.policy = "latency-preferred"
redwood.route.fallback = "cpu-quant"
redwood.request.priority = "tier-1"
request.id = "req_xxx"
```
I used a vendor prefix `redwood.` to avoid colliding with OTEL common keys. Numbers should be numeric where possible.

Sylvia Park: prefer shorter keys for dashboards (less wide columns in BigQuery). What about `model.name` instead of `redwood.model.name`? Also concerned about leaking exact prompt text — don't include prompt or completion text in spans. Token counts ok.

Matt R: Agree on avoiding raw text. About prefix: pros/cons — vendor prefix avoids collisions and makes it obvious these are Redwood semantic attrs. But it makes queries longer. Maybe compromise: use `model.name` and `model.version` but set `telemetry.source = "redwood"` and `service.name` already identifies us.

Priya Singh: Problem: customers might self-host telemetry or forward to their sinks. If we use unprefixed keys we risk collisions with downstream teams. On the other hand, tracing back to Redwood is redundant because service.name is present. Leaning toward `model.*` for ergonomics.

telemetry-bot: FYI — OTEL spec recommends using stable keys and avoiding PII. Also suggests using dotted keys for grouping. See https://opentelemetry.io/docs/reference/specification/trace/semantic_conventions/ (link) :information_source:

Amy Chen: OK can we agree on a concrete list we can put in the SDK? My proposal (compromise):
```
span.name = "redwood.infer.request"        # root span at API ingress
service.name = "redwood-inference"
model.name = ""                            # e.g. gpt-4o-mini
model.version = ""                         # semantic stable version
model.variant = ""                         # int8, fp16
tokens.request = 0                           # integer
tokens.generated = 0                         # integer
cache.hit = false                            # boolean
routing.policy = ""                        # latency/cost/region
route.fallback = ""                        # fallback target if any
request.priority = ""                      # tier name
request.id = ""                            # opaque request id
error = false                                # boolean, true if error
http.status_code = 200                       # if applicable
```
Keep keys short but unambiguous. We'll namespace any vendor-specific experimental attrs with `redwood.*` (e.g., `redwood.batch.size`, `redwood.kv_cache.prefix_hit`).

Matt R: +1. Also propose we include `instrumentation.scope.name = "redwood.sdk"` in the SDK so downstream can filter by our SDK version.

Priya Singh: sampling thoughts — we should keep full traces for errors and for expensive models (>100ms p50 for generate). For normal traffic use a head-based sampler with dynamic tail-sampling to keep sample rate per model. Also keep metrics derived from spans (counts, p50/p95/p99) for 90 days, raw traces 14 days, and aggregated headers/attributes 90 days. Cost estimation: raw traces retention above 7 days will be expensive for high-volume customers.

Sylvia Park: add `cache.hit` -> store as boolean and also `cache.ttl_seconds` only when a hit occurred? That helps cache effectiveness dashboards.

Amy Chen: Noted. On exporters: we will send OTLP/HTTP to our collector with a transform that renames `request.id` -> `redwood.request.id` to avoid collisions in downstream metrics. Collector will also drop `prompt.*` keys and any attr with substring `prompt`/`user_text` for PII safety.

Matt R: Implementation plan for SDK: 
- default span name as agreed
- auto-populate model.* + tokens.* + cache.hit if runtime has those values
- add opt-in debug mode to attach `redwood.trace.payload_size` (bytes)
- expose env vars: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING, REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_EXPORTERS

Priya Singh: tiny note: prefer `tokens.input`/`tokens.output` over `tokens.request`/`tokens.generated`? More semantic. Minor.

Amy Chen: let's finalize naming: tokens.input/tokens.output, model.name/version/variant, cache.hit, routing.policy, route.fallback, request.id. Action items: 1) Matt to PR SDK defaults (due EOD Fri). 2) Priya to write sampling policy doc + retention cost estimates. 3) Sylvia to update collector transform rules. 4) I will create dashboards mapping old keys to new keys for a month.

Matt R: working on PR now, will cc the SDK reviewers. :rocket:

Sylvia Park: I'll add a collector test to assert PII redaction.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: meeting 11am Thu to review telemetry rollout. Added to thread. :calendar:

Amy Chen: thanks everyone — will follow up with a short RFC that includes the final JSON schema for attributes (so external infra teams can adopt).
